docs.title: vergil-fixture-ts-app
docs.text:
This is a Vergil test fixture. It has no users.

It holds a small TypeScript command-line application so that Vergil's support for TypeScript applications runs against a real one: local validation with vrg-validate, the build, CI, the dependency and license audit, this docs site and the tagged release. Each fixture run adds one small increment to the program and drives it through Vergil's full cycle, from change to release.

Why the fixture exists, and how a fixture run works, is set out in the spec of epic vergil-project/.github#1091. The TypeScript fixtures came with epic vergil-project/.github#1174.

docs.title: What it exercises
docs.text:
• vrg-validate's TypeScript checks: the required devDependencies at their accepted majors, Prettier and ESLint on Vergil's managed configs, tsc, Vitest at 100% line coverage, npm audit and the license summary, and the BUILD check, which compiles the program to dist/.
  • Two real runtime dependencies, commander and zod, for the audit and the dependency tooling to work on.
  • The fleet's CI and CD workflows, this site and the release.

Nothing it builds is published to a package registry.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: The fixture is an npm package, private to the repo, with one binary, vergil-fixture-ts-app. It needs Node.js 24 or later.

docs.title: Build and run
docs.text:
From a clone of the repository:

$ npm ci --ignore-scripts
$ npm run build
$ node dist/main.js greet Ada
Hello, Ada

npm run build compiles src/ to dist/ with tsconfig.build.json, and dist/main.js is the binary the package's bin entry names.

docs.title: Validate
docs.text:
As in every Vergil repo, validation runs in the Vergil dev container, and nothing else is the gate:

vrg-container-run -- vrg-validate

docs.title: Layout
docs.text: Path Holds src/main.ts the binary: run the program on the process's arguments and set its exit code src/cli.ts buildProgram, the commander parser, and run, which returns the exit code src/context.ts the Io and Context a subcommand is given, and CommandError src/commands/ one module per subcommand, and index.ts, which lists them src/integers.ts the zod parser for integer arguments src/metadata.ts the program's name and version, read from package.json test/ the Vitest tests, which cover every line of src/

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
File Holds tsconfig.json extends Vergil's managed tsconfig.vergil.json; type-checks src/ and test/ tsconfig.build.json the build: src/ only, emitted to dist/ eslint.config.mjs spreads Vergil's managed eslint.vergil.config.mjs vitest.config.ts the test files, and coverage measured over src/

tsconfig.vergil.json, eslint.vergil.config.mjs and .prettierrc.json are written by Vergil's fleet sync. They are never edited here.

docs.title: Adding a subcommand
docs.text:
A fixture run grows the program by one subcommand at a time, with no restructuring:

  1. Add src/commands/<name>.ts with the subcommand's logic as a plain exported function and a register(program, context) that adds the command and writes the result through context.io. A failure the user should see throws a CommandError.
  2. Add the module to subcommands in src/commands/index.ts.
  3. Add its tests under test/, its entry to the Usage page, and its row to the subcommand table in the repository's README.md.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
vergil-fixture-ts-app [options] [command]
Command Prints greet NAME a greeting for NAME sum [NUMBERS...] the sum of the integers max NUMBERS... the largest of the integers min NUMBERS... the smallest of the integers reverse TEXT TEXT with its characters reversed length TEXT the number of characters in TEXT upper TEXT TEXT in upper case lower TEXT TEXT in lower case info the program's name and version as JSON

--help (-h) prints the commands, and --version (-V) prints the program's version. Each command takes --help too.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Code Meaning 0 success, --help and --version included 1 a usage error, or the command failed; the reason is on standard error, after error:

With no command, the program prints its usage on standard error and exits 1.

docs.title: greet
docs.text:
$ vergil-fixture-ts-app greet Ada
Hello, Ada

NAME is required.

docs.title: sum
docs.text:
$ vergil-fixture-ts-app sum 1 2 -4
-1
$ vergil-fixture-ts-app sum
0

Each number is a decimal integer with an optional sign, within JavaScript's safe integer range (±9007199254740991). Anything else is a usage error that names the value:

$ vergil-fixture-ts-app sum 1 two
error: command-argument value 'two' is invalid for argument 'numbers'. not an integer

A sum outside the safe integer range fails rather than print a rounded result:

$ vergil-fixture-ts-app sum 9007199254740991 1
error: the sum is out of the safe integer range

docs.title: max
docs.text:
$ vergil-fixture-ts-app max 1 7 -4
7

At least one number is required. Each is a decimal integer within the same safe range as for sum, and anything else is a usage error that names the value:

$ vergil-fixture-ts-app max 1 x
error: command-argument value 'x' is invalid for argument 'numbers'. not an integer

docs.title: min
docs.text:
$ vergil-fixture-ts-app min 1 -4 7
-4

At least one number is required. Each is a decimal integer within the same safe range as for sum, and anything else is a usage error that names the value:

$ vergil-fixture-ts-app min x 1
error: command-argument value 'x' is invalid for argument 'numbers'. not an integer

docs.title: reverse
docs.text:
$ vergil-fixture-ts-app reverse "Ada Lovelace"
ecalevoL adA

TEXT is required. Each character is a user-perceived character (a grapheme cluster), so an accented letter written with a combining mark, or an emoji made of several code points, stays whole.

docs.title: length
docs.text:
$ vergil-fixture-ts-app length "Ada Lovelace"
12

TEXT is required. Characters are counted as for reverse: each is a user-perceived character (a grapheme cluster), so an accented letter written with a combining mark, or an emoji made of several code points, counts as one.

docs.title: upper
docs.text:
$ vergil-fixture-ts-app upper "Ada Lovelace"
ADA LOVELACE

TEXT is required. It is converted by Unicode's default case mapping, the same in every locale, so a letter can become more than one: straße prints as STRASSE.

docs.title: lower
docs.text:
$ vergil-fixture-ts-app lower "Ada Lovelace"
ada lovelace

TEXT is required. It is converted by Unicode's default case mapping, the same in every locale, so a capital sigma that ends a word takes the final form: ΟΔΟΣ prints as οδος.

docs.title: info
docs.text:
$ vergil-fixture-ts-app info
{"name":"vergil-fixture-ts-app","version":"0.1.0"}

The name and version are those in the package's package.json.
